title: Snippet Governance, Telemetry & Canonical-Fix Runbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This runbook defines the governance, telemetry contract, and canonical-fix release workflow for code snippets and API examples published in the developer docs site. It is intended for doc owners, SDK maintainers, developer advocates, and support engineers who triage snippet-related issues.

Goals

- Ensure snippets are discoverable, reliable, and minimized for drift.
- Provide a deterministic rollback and patch path for broken snippets (canonical fixes) exposed to customers.
- Maintain a telemetry contract so support and eng can quickly map a failing example to the code and test vector that produced it.

Scope

Applies to: all code snippets, SDK examples, and small runnable manifests that live under "eng-developer-experience" docs-site and quickstarts folders. Excluded: internal-only prototype drafts in Google Drive.

Ownership and Roles

- Snippet Owner: the engineer or writer who authored the snippet (explicit in snippet header).
- Patch Owner: the SDK/Runtime team owning the upstream API surface affected.
- Docs Site Owner: eng-developer-experience docs lead (see table below).
- On-call Support: devx-support rotation.

Table: Primary owners

| Area | Responsible | Escalation | Contact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript SDK snippets | SDK JS Team | SDK JS Lead | sdk-js@redwood.example.com |
| Python SDK snippets | SDK Python Team | SDK Py Lead | sdk-py@redwood.example.com |
| API examples / cURL | DevX Docs | Docs Lead | devx-docs@redwood.example.com |

Snippet metadata standards

Every snippet file must include a YAML header comment block with the following fields:

---
snippet_id: "docs-site-snippet-<space>-<short-key>-v1"
owner: "Full Name <team-email>"
verified: "yes|no"
last_tested: "YYYY-MM-DD"
telemetry_key: "snippet.telemetry:<uuid>"
---

Example header (JavaScript):

/*
snippet_id: docs-site-snippet-js-auth-flow-v1
owner: Asha Patel <sdk-js@redwood.example.com>
verified: yes
last_tested: 2025-02-10
telemetry_key: snippet.telemetry:9f2c5b2a-4b3a-4d2b-8d1e-ae8b1f2d3c4e
*/

Telemetry contract (minimal)

All snippet executions in automated smoke runs and customer-facing telemetry must emit the following JSON payload to our docs-snippet telemetry ingestion endpoint (/internal/api/v1/telemetry/snippets). Keys and types are strict:

{
  "telemetry_key": "string", // snippet.telemetry:<uuid>
  "snippet_id": "string",
  "example_language": "string", // e.g. js, py, curl
  "sdk_version": "string",
  "doc_version": "string", // semver of docs site packaging
  "execution_timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "run_result": "string", // success | error | timeout | flake
  "error_class": "string", // optional
  "error_message": "string", // optional, truncated to 1024 chars
  "trace_id": "string" // optional, cross-system correlation
}

Note: the ingestion endpoint rejects payloads missing telemetry_key or snippet_id with HTTP 400.

Canonical-fix workflow (high-level)

1) Detection
   - Automatic: nightly smoke runs (all runnable snippets) report failure to telemetry and open an auto-ticket in the Snippet Bugboard.
   - Manual: customers or support file tickets with snippet.telemetry:<uuid> in logs.

2) Triage (SLA: 8 business hours)
   - Support labels ticket with "snippet-failure" and attaches telemetry payload.
   - Docs Site Owner triages to identify whether fix is: documentation-only, snippet patch, or SDK bug.

3) Patch path selection
   - Doc-only fix: modify snippet, bump snippet header last_tested, submit PR against docs repo using the snippet patch template.
   - SDK fix: assign to Patch Owner; if release required, follow SDK patch-release-playbook.
   - Temporary workaround: update snippet to include a guarded example and add a deprecation note.

4) Canonical-fix PR requirements
   - PR title must include the snippet_id and telemetry_key.
   - Include failing telemetry payload and smoke run link in PR description.
   - Add reviewer from the owning SDK or Docs team.
   - Must include a regression test (example-level unit or smoke test) that runs in CI.

5) Release and Monitoring
   - Merge triggers docs site canary publish to a staging channel.
   - Smoke test pipeline must re-run the fixed snippet; telemetry should report run_result: success.
   - If the fix targets an SDK release, the SDK must publish a patch and docs reference updated to pinned sdk_version.

Rollback procedure (when a published fix introduces regressions)

1) Revert the canonical-fix PR in docs repo (fast path).
2) If multiple changes were merged, create a targeted revert that only touches affected snippet files.
3) For SDK regressions, revert the SDK patch release and re-open the SDK patch ticket.
4) Notify stakeholders: docs@, sdk-team, customer-success.

Operational run commands

- Trigger full runnable-snippet smoke run (docs repo CI):
  ./tools/run-snippet-smoke.sh --all --staging

- Re-run single snippet by id:
  ./tools/run-snippet-smoke.sh --id docs-site-snippet-js-auth-flow-v1 --local

- Submit telemetry replay for debugging (privileged):
  curl -s -X POST https://internal.redwood.example.com/internal/api/v1/telemetry/replay \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPLAY_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"telemetry_key":"snippet.telemetry:9f2c5b2a-4b3a-4d2b-8d1e-ae8b1f2d3c4e", "since":"2025-02-10T00:00:00Z" }'

SLOs and metrics

- Mean time to resolution (MTTR) for snippet failures: 3 business days for doc-only fixes, 7 business days for SDK fixes.
- Smoke-run coverage: >= 95% of runnable snippets executed nightly.
- Telemetry ingestion success rate: 99.5%

Common canonical-fix templates and examples

1) Doc-only: small API param rename
   - PR must include before/after snippet and an inline note explaining change.

2) API shape change requiring SDK patch
   - Patch Owner must publish SDK patch and update snippet header pinned sdk_version.

3) Flaky external dependency (token rotation, network)
   - Add retry guidance in snippet and mark verified: no; add remediation steps in PR.

Troubleshooting checklist

- If telemetry missing: verify snippet header telemetry_key present and CI runner has TELEMETRY_WRITE key.
- If smoke runs pass locally but fail in CI: confirm container image versions and network egress rules for CI runners.
- If error_message truncated: check ingestion service logs; file bug with telemetry team.

Appendix: Example canonical-fix PR description

Title: Fix: docs-site-snippet-js-auth-flow-v1 (snippet.telemetry:9f2c5b2a) - handle new token shape

Description:
- Failing telemetry: [link]
- Smoke run: https://ci.redwood.example.com/builds/45678
- Root cause: SDK changed auth token field from accessToken -> token.value
- Change: update snippet to use token.value and add fallback for accessToken.
- Regression test: tools/tests/snippets/test_js_auth_flow.py::test_auth_flow

Sign-off: @sdk-js-lead, @devx-docs

Related pages and references
